overview: Black develops the c8-bishop to g4 immediately, pinning the Nf3, and White continues with Bg2 and O-O, h3 and d3, aiming for the usual King's Indian Attack structure. After 3.Bg2 Nd7 Black will play ...e6 or ...c6 and a solid set-up. The play is slow, flexible and positional, with White aiming for e4.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bg2, O-O, d3 and Nbd2
Drive the bishop away with h3 and play e4

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Nd7, ...e6, ...c6 and pin the knight

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian Attack structure with pawns on d3, e4 against d5/e6/c6

character.notes: Steady and manoeuvring; neither side has an early attack.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; White's e4 break still to come, flexible.

approach.notes: The KIA is a set-up White can play against almost anything.

level.notes: Plans are clear but need practice to play well.

character.reason: Quiet slow play, not sharp but not especially solid either.

approach.reason: White's KIA set-up is played against many replies.

level.reason: Clear set-up, but the timing needs experience.

plans.reason: Fianchetto on g2 is the main idea.
